newsitem.title: UK: Rolls considers new engine for Airbus A340.
newsitem.headline: Rolls considers new engine for Airbus A340.

text.p: Aero-engine manufacturer Rolls-Royce Plc said on Thursday it was looking at the idea of developing the new engine needed by Airbus Industrie for the planned stretch version of its A340 widebody jet.
"It's under active consideration, as a design exercise," chairman Ralph Robins told Reuters in an interview.
He said nothing was decided yet but there could be some news on the plans later this year. "One might see something happen during the spring or summer."

However, although Rolls could mitigate the cost of developing another engine by basing it on its big new Trent turbofan, the company would still need a bigger market than just the A340 to justify the cost, he said.
He said the company was looking also keeping an eye on proposals by Boeing to introduce bigger versions of the 747-400 and the 767 twinjet.
"We are looking at an engine that will drive the A340, 747-400 growth and the 767-400 if it was to happen."
"I have always said you don't get much for a billion dollars out of a big engine development like the Trent," he said, when asked how much Trent cost.
"But we do have some very interesting ideas based on our Trent (engine) core and our ability to mix and match Trent technology and Trent components."
Because it would be a derivative any new engine was likely to be developed "at a much more predictable cost, at a much more moderate cost than one might think for a new engine."
"We think we can make a very attractive machine for the A340," he said.
